jobs.title: Director and Technical Lead Data Science & Innovation GEMINI
jobs.description:
GEMINI is Canada’s largest hospital data and analytics network that provides insight into patient care for research and quality improvement. Currently, GEMINI holds granular data on >3 million patient admissions (>10 billion data points) – a population-level laboratory to study and improve hospital care. This deep individual-level data is critical to harness advanced analytic methods such as artificial intelligence and machine learning.

GEMINI uses advanced methods and analytics to extract and standardize data captured in hospital electronic health records. Over 1,000 scientists, clinicians, and students are increasingly using this data. GEMINI currently exists at 40+ Ontario hospitals and supports the Ontario General Medicine Quality Improvement Network, GeMQIN, a provincial network led by Ontario Health to improve care for general medicine hospital patients. In total, GEMINI has been a core dataset on >$300 million of grant funding across 20 institutions.

Building on GEMINI, the Government of Canada has funded the establishment of Vital, a national-scale data platform to enable research and innovation with near real-time hospital data from at least 8 provinces and territories, beginning with Ontario, Alberta and Quebec.

The Technical Lead and Director, GEMINI Data Science and Innovation will lead GEMINI’s efforts in accelerating research and innovation using hospital data by leveraging technology, optimizing processes and streamlining operations, and implementing data governance approaches. The Director will lead the continued growth and successful development of GEMINI’s data and analytics platform. An important part of the work, to be accomplished in partnership with the Technical Lead for Vital, will be to lead the establishment of the capabilities that are required for Ontario’s participation in the new national Vital platform.

The successful candidate will have expertise in data management, a strong technical background, and experience leading a technical team. They will promote a safe and inclusive work environment and lead an agile and cross-functional team that works in data collection and management, reporting, research software, and data analytics. They will work closely with a supportive systems and IT infrastructure team, particularly in the implementation of cybersecurity tools and practices, as well as with a research operations team that is responsible for setting data governance and privacy policies, which the data team implements. They will build strong positive relationships with GEMINI’s internal and external stakeholders including hospital leadership, researchers and government partners. They will participate in the Executive Team of the Unity Health Toronto GEMINI and Vital teams, providing strategic input into organizational direction and management.

Duties And Responsibilities

Provide strategic leadership, set priorities and operational oversight to advance GEMINI’s data and analytics platform.
Promote innovation and lead efforts to develop novel approaches to tackle data challenges.
Manage and advance GEMINI’s established data collection, standardization, and quality control processes, including initiatives to modernize data assets through the implementation of common data models that support scalable research, analytics, and interoperability.
Provide strategic and operational oversight of the GeMQIN reporting program, ensuring the timely delivery of high-quality reports that meet the needs of participating hospitals and support quality improvement initiatives.
Oversee the technical ecosystem that supports research use of GEMINI data, including research-ready databases and analytics tools, ensuring solutions are scalable, maintainable, secure, and aligned with organizational priorities.
Work with the Vital Technical Lead to innovate new methods in hospital data collection to enable near real-time access to data for research and innovation.
Lead the implementation of technology and processes to implement data governance and privacy practices, ensuring regulatory compliance of GEMINI’s data holdings and infrastructure, in partnership with the research operations team.
Work with the IT systems and research operations team to implement cybersecurity technology and practices for handling sensitive health data.
Work with GEMINI’s research team to incorporate new innovations, particularly harnessing Artificial Intelligence, into routine data collection and management processes and into analytical tools.
Work with GEMINI’s research team to support the development and delivery of data products and analytical tools to facilitate efficient, cutting-edge research.
Manage and execute processes that support the continuous improvement of data team operations.
Lead the GEMINI data platform team through a period of transition relating to new methods of data collection and processing and new ways of engaging with the national Vital network.
Provide strategic input into organizational decision-making for GEMINI and Vital that is grounded in data and analytic expertise.
Lead multidisciplinary technical teams across data collection, reporting, data engineering, analytics, data science, and research software development.
Foster a positive work culture that encourages innovation, learning and continuous improvement, supported by the broader Executive Team within GEMINI and Vital and Unity Health Toronto, as well as external expert coaching as needed.
Contribute to strategic decisions about team structure and human resources for the GEMINI data team to optimize team function, aligned with GEMINI’s evolving deliverables, including identifying capacity needs and supporting recruitment and retention of team members.
Provide mentorship, coaching and growth opportunities to a diverse workforce, with a particular focus on technical mentorship, supporting team members to upskill and improve their workflows with AI and rapidly evolving computing technologies.
Work collaboratively with GEMINI leaders and other stakeholders including hospital leadership, researchers and government partners.

Qualifications

Completion of a Master’s degree in Computer Science, Bioinformatics and/or related discipline; PhD an asset
Minimum seven (7) years of experience conducting and leading data-driven initiatives and large-scale projects
Minimum seven (7) years of relevant experience participating in and managing cross-functional teams with the ability to guide teams through complex projects, ambiguity, and change
Minimum seven (7) years of experience across multiple technical domains, including data engineering, data management, data analytics and reporting, data science, artificial intelligence, software development, and data governance
Minimum five (5) years of experience with healthcare data including clinical and operational workflows
Minimum five (5) plus years of experience using project management tools and methodologies
Outstanding analytical and problem-solving skills
Strong experience working with high performance computing environments, complex technical operations and software development principles in an open source framework
Advanced knowledge in data science tools such as R and Python, and relational databases
Familiarity with cloud-based infrastructure, federated analysis and event-driven architecture is an asset
Exceptional organization skills and strong time management experience developing project plans to meet objectives and budgets, adaptable to managing multiple tasks and deadline pressures
Exceptional written and oral communication skills to engage, articulate and conceptualize ideas/issues at all organizational levels with stakeholders
Fully proficient in working independently and self-directed while taking accountability for own actions

The Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) team is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technologies and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada, but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

This is a hybrid role with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

Role Vision and Impact

The Senior Director, Information Security and End-User Technology, serves as CBC/Radio-Canada’s Chief Information Security Officer (CISO). A strategic, visionary and collaborative leader, the CISO defines, implements and drives the overarching vision for cybersecurity, risk management and technological resilience across all corporate environments.

The mission of this strategic role is to protect information assets, data, digital heritage, and production and broadcasting infrastructure across all platforms, while ensuring seamless, agile and uninterrupted media operations.
The Senior Director optimally balances rigorous security architecture governance with the flexibility that creative, journalistic and technical teams need to innovate and broadcast without disruption.

Operating at a senior executive level, the CISO regularly briefs and advises the Board of Directors (BoD),
the Audit Committee,
the CBC/Radio-Canada Senior Executive Team (SET)
and the T&I Management Executive Team (MET).

Supported by a team of experienced directors and senior managers overseeing governance, security operations, end-user technology and identity management, the Senior Director serves as the cornerstone of digital trust and strategic transformation for Canada’s public broadcaster.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Vision, Leadership and Executive Relations

Develop, champion and execute an enterprise-wide cybersecurity strategy aligned with the Corporation’s business mission, risk profile and digital transformation.
Serve as a trusted expert and strategic adviser to the BoD, Audit Committee, SET and MET regarding risk status, security posture and maturity, and required investments.
Foster a “Security by Design” culture and establish security architecture governance frameworks that keep operational and production workflows running smoothly while proactively managing risk.
Anticipate technology trends and lead the secure integration of artificial intelligence (AI/GenAI) and automation into business processes and security defences across the organization.

Securing IT, Cloud, Distribution and Broadcast/Operational Technology (OT) Environments

Define and continuously adapt the security strategy across the entire technology landscape, including corporate IT infrastructure, cloud systems, end-user environments, and critical production, broadcast and network infrastructure.
Ensure the resilience of content acquisition, processing and distribution workflows against threats targeting the media sector and critical infrastructure.

Governance, Risk, Compliance and AI Governance

Oversee the governance function responsible for developing, maintaining and enforcing policies, standards, security architecture principles, exception management and industry frameworks (e.g., NIST, ISO 27001, AI frameworks).
Lead the third-party and partner risk management program (covering vendors and technology contracts) in close collaboration with the Legal Services and Procurement teams.
Co-develop a governance, compliance and ethical framework for the enterprise-wide use of AI and generative AI, assessing specific risks throughout their life cycle.
Ensure strict compliance with applicable laws and regulations (e.g., Quebec’s Law 25, GDPR and sector-specific requirements).
Drive a cybersecurity culture and awareness program focused on lasting behaviour change across the organization.

Defence Operations, SOC and Crisis Management

Oversee the performance and modernization of the Security Operations Centre (SOC), advanced detection tools (SIEM, EDR/XDR, automation) and continuous threat monitoring.
Direct major security incident response operations and lead technology crisis management, from detection to full business recovery.
Oversee regular penetration testing, vulnerability assessments and cyberattack simulation exercises across IT, broadcast and distribution environments.

Identity and End-User Technology

Guide the strategic vision for Identity and Access Management (IAM, PAM) to provide secure, simple and frictionless access for all staff and contractors.
Collaborate closely with the End-User Technology teams to align security with a modern, efficient and intuitive employee experience.

Financial Management and Team Engagement

Inspire, coach and develop a team of directors and senior managers — fostering excellence, innovation and cross-functional collaboration.
Lead with the heart.

Education and Certifications

Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, cybersecurity, computer engineering, business administration (IT concentration) or a related field.
At least one recognized executive-level professional certification: CISSP, CISM, CCISO, CISA or CRISC.

Professional Experience

Seven to 10 years of experience managing professional teams or equivalent.
Deep expertise in technology architecture, cloud security, network infrastructure, cryptography, and identity and access management (IAM).
Ability to provide collaborative leadership within the organization to see complex, transformational initiatives through to completion.
Demonstrated skills in planning, organizing and engaging teams.
Proven ability and track record in leading cross-functional teams.
Proven ability to work with cross-functional, agile teams or on projects that have multi-team dependencies.
Ability to distil complex issues into clear, concise presentations and reports.
Expertise in the various technologies typically used by journalists in a newsroom.
Knowledge of business practices, including drafting plans and specifications, contracts, negotiation, finance, and IT management software.
Knowledge of software development and the technology infrastructure required for product delivery.
Knowledge of workflows for content acquisition, management and distribution, with a focus on storytelling.

Leadership

Leads, develops, coaches and mentors a high-performing team to deliver and exceed expectations while coaching employees to realize their professional development goals

Receives and resolves escalated and complex matters by referral from team members and business partners
Maintains current and relevant knowledge of industry trends, accounting standards, regulatory environment, competitor products and strategies
Builds a values aligned culture that supports the execution of change initiatives
Accountable for ongoing department efficiency through automation and process improvements
Acts as an ambassador of ACU by being visible in the organization and the community in support of corporate and community initiatives
Champions ACU’s commitment to values-based banking, respectful workplace and diversity and inclusion

Guides the production of support documents and files for monthly and year-end financial statements, audited statements and regulatory reports
Oversees the analysis of economic, business and financial conditions and their impact on the ACU’s operations; makes recommendations as appropriate to enhance performance or to mitigate losses

Safeguards the credit union assets by continually monitoring routines to ensure accurate controls for general ledger and subsidiary systems
Ensures records maintenance meets the requirements of regulatory bodies and the Privacy Act and that an effective system is in place to monitor retention and disposal of all records

Operational Planning & Execution

Develops and implements business cases, operational and execution plans required to advance ACU’s strategic commitments to cultivate profitable growth, drive operational excellence, propel social impact, and foster organizational capabilities through a knowledgeable and capable team
Contributes to corporate strategic and operational planning through the provision of financial information, analysis, projections and recommendations

Understands the intricate complexities of the business and the credit union system and is knowledgeable in ACU’s current products, services, operations philosophies and principles

puts people, planet and prosperity first,

is committed to serving its urban, rural, agricultural, and Francophone communities,
is focused on social and environmental responsibility,
